s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of unilateral lower extremity numbness, pain, and weakness, with progression to foot drop, without significant low back pain
salient_findings: Foot drop with significant weakness of tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, flexor hallucis longus, and peroneus longus
key_facts: 48-year-old woman with a history of asthma
2-day history of right lower-extremity numbness and pain
No low back pain
Manual muscle testing showed weakness of right tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus
Deep-tendon reflexes were normal initially
Straight-leg-raising was positive at 70 degrees
Femoral-nerve stretch test was negative
Lumbar MRI showed right-sided disc herniation at L5-S1 without significant nerve-root or cord compression
Peroneal-nerve conduction studies showed decreased motor conduction velocity
Ankle-brachial indices were decreased
Lower-extremity arteriography showed no significant vascular lesions
Symptoms worsened despite initial improvement with treatment

shortlist.label: L5 radiculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Initial presentation with right lower-extremity numbness and pain, and subsequent development of foot drop, is consistent with L5 radiculopathy

shortlist.label: Peroneal nerve palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Weakness of peroneal-innervated muscles and decreased motor conduction velocity on peroneal-nerve conduction studies support peroneal nerve palsy

shortlist.label: Lumbosacral plexopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Progression of symptoms and involvement of multiple nerve roots suggest lumbosacral plexopathy

shortlist.label: Fibular neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Foot drop and weakness of muscles innervated by the fibular nerve are consistent with fibular neuropathy

shortlist.label: Cauda equina syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral absence of Achilles reflexes and progression of symptoms despite initial improvement suggest cauda equina syndrome as a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of right lower-extremity numbness and pain, weakness of the tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus, and decreased motor conduction velocity on peroneal-nerve conduction studies are consistent with peroneal nerve palsy. The development of right foot drop and absent Achilles reflexes also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: L5 radiculopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a disc herniation at L5-S1, the lack of significant nerve-root compression on MRI and the specific pattern of weakness and pain suggest a more distal lesion.

rejected.label: Lumbosacral plexopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are more localized to the peroneal nerve distribution, and there is no evidence of a more widespread plexopathy.

rejected.label: Fibular neuropathy
rejected.why: Fibular neuropathy is a subset of peroneal nerve palsy, and the patient's symptoms are consistent with a more proximal peroneal nerve lesion.

rejected.label: Cauda equina syndrome
rejected.why: The patient does not have the typical symptoms of cauda equina syndrome, such as bilateral leg weakness, saddle anesthesia, or bowel/bladder dysfunction.
